day-1.t: Day 1 — Pick a niche you can actually serve

b.v: Today's goal

v: Choose one clear group of customers to serve
Write down what they already buy and where they buy it
Say no to at least two niches that do not fit you

b.v: About 20 minutes. Keep a notes app or a notebook open.

Most new stores die before the first sale because they sell a little of everything. A stranger landing on a shop that sells phone cases, abayas and kitchen knives does not trust it. One clear customer is easier to reach, easier to write for, and easier to remember.
1) What a niche really means
A niche is a small, specific group of people with a shared problem. It is not a product category. It is a person plus a need.

v: Not a niche = gifts, clothes and mobile accessories
A niche = school teachers in Karachi buying cheap classroom rewards
A niche = new mothers in Lahore looking for affordable baby bedding
A niche = small cafe owners in Islamabad who need takeaway cups

b.v: 2) Test the niche in fifteen minutes
You do not need paid tools. You need to see people already spending money in this area. Facebook groups and WhatsApp communities show you that for free.

Do this search test:|Open Facebook and search your niche words plus your city|Note how many groups exist and how many members the biggest has|Read the last twenty comments and look for complaints|Write down the three complaints you saw most often
3) Check that you can supply it
A niche you cannot supply is a hobby, not a store. Before you commit, answer three boring questions about stock and time.

v: Can you get the product locally within a week?
Can you describe it honestly in your own words?
Would you still answer a WhatsApp message about it at 11 pm?

b.v: Do not pick a niche only because a video said it makes money. The person in the video is selling a course about the niche, not the niche itself.
Practice
Write one sentence under 25 words: I sell ____ to ____ in ____ who want ____. If you cannot finish it, the niche is still too wide.

day-2.t: Day 2 — Find products without fantasy maths

b.v: Today's goal

v: Build a list of five possible products
Calculate real cost per unit including delivery and returns
Drop any product that only works on paper

b.v: About 25 minutes. A simple calculator is enough.
Beginners count the buying price and stop. Then the first return, the first failed delivery and the first ad bill arrive, and the profit disappears. Today you count everything.
1) Where to look for products
Good products solve a small annoying problem and are hard to find in a local shop. Look where demand already shows, not where suppliers advertise.

v: Local wholesale markets and their WhatsApp catalogues
Daraz best seller lists, to see what people already search
Facebook group complaints, which are free product ideas
Physical shops in your city, to check the retail price you must beat

b.v: 2) Count the true cost of one order
Take one product and write the numbers down. If the margin after everything is thin, no amount of good design will save it.

Calculate like this:|Product cost from supplier, including any delivery to you|Packaging: box, tape, bubble wrap, thank you slip|Delivery to the customer, at the rate you will actually pay|Return allowance: assume some parcels come back|Payment or platform fee, at the current rate|Subtract the total from your selling price
Do not assume a 0 percent return rate. In cash on delivery selling, some parcels are refused at the door. Put a return allowance in the maths from day one.
3) Score the product, do not fall in love with it
Rate every idea on the same four points so you compare fairly instead of choosing the one you like most.

v: Weight = light parcels cost less to send
Breakability = glass and liquids cause returns
Repeat purchase = does the customer come back
Explanation = can a photo and three lines sell it

b.v: Practice
Pick your best product and write its full cost sheet on paper. Then write the lowest price you can sell it for and still keep a real margin.

day-3.t: Day 3 — Set up the account and the store basics

b.v: Today's goal

v: Create the store and finish the basic settings
Set the currency, time zone and store name properly
Choose a free theme and know why

b.v: About 25 minutes. A laptop is easier, but the phone app works.

Shopify is a hosted store builder. You pay a monthly subscription and it handles hosting, security and updates. At the time of writing there is usually a short free trial, and the plan prices change, so check the current price on their pricing page before you commit.
1) Create the account without mistakes
The email you sign up with becomes the owner. Use a business email you will keep, not a temporary one.

Sign up:|Go to the Shopify website and start the free trial|Use a real email and a strong password|Answer the setup questions honestly about your experience|Skip any paid add-on offered during signup|Open Settings and set store name, currency to PKR, and your time zone
2) Choose a free theme and stop
A theme is the design template. Free themes are fast and clean. Paid themes do not fix a weak product page.

v: Pick one of the free themes built for your product count
Keep the default colours on day one
Upload a simple logo, 500 pixels wide is enough
Do not install five apps before your first order

b.v: Do not spend your first week choosing colours. A plain store with honest photos and clear prices sells better than a beautiful store with unclear delivery charges.
3) Set the boring settings now
These settings cause support messages later if you skip them. Ten minutes now saves hours of WhatsApp arguments.

v: Store address and phone number, visible on the contact page
Order notification email, and check it actually arrives
Weight units in kilograms if you will ship locally
Tax settings, usually off for small local sellers, but confirm with your accountant

b.v: Practice
Create the store, set the currency to PKR, install one free theme and place a test order for yourself. Then cancel and refund that test order.

day-4.t: Day 4 — Build collections that make sense

b.v: Today's goal

v: Understand products versus collections
Create two or three collections a customer can understand
Add your first three products with correct data

b.v: About 20 minutes. Have your product photos ready.
A product is one item. A collection is a group of products, like a shelf in a shop. Messy collections make the store feel like a storeroom, and shoppers leave.
1) Start with products
Add the product once, then let collections pick it up automatically. Typing product names into collections by hand creates duplicates later.

Add a product:|Products, then Add product|Write a clear title, brand first if there is one|Set price and compare at price only if the higher price was real|Add the weight in kilograms|Upload at least three photos, square and well lit|Write a short description and save
2) Use automatic collections
An automatic collection fills itself using a rule, for example all products tagged bedding. A manual collection needs you to add each item by hand.

v: Tag every product with two or three simple words
Build collections from those tags
Keep the menu to five links or fewer
Name collections the way customers speak, not the way suppliers speak

b.v: Do not create a collection with one product in it. An almost empty shelf looks like a closing down sale.
3) Connect the menu
The menu is the map of your store. If a customer cannot reach a product in two taps, treat it as missing.

Build the menu:|Online Store, then Navigation|Edit the main menu|Add Shop All first, then your two or three collections|Add Contact and Delivery and Returns|Save and open your store on your own phone to check
Practice
Add three real products with weights and photos, tag them, and create one automatic collection from those tags. Then open the store on your phone and buy nothing, just look.
Today's goal

v: Write a product page that answers the buyer's real questions
Place delivery and return information above the button
Rewrite one page today

b.v: About 25 minutes. Open one of your own product pages.
Traffic is expensive. A product page is free and it decides whether that traffic becomes money. The job of the page is not to describe the product. It is to remove doubt.
1) Answer the four doubts
Every shopper has the same four silent questions. Answer them on the page and you stop losing people who were ready to buy.

v: What exactly will arrive in the box?
How long will delivery take to my city?
What if it is damaged or the wrong size?
Can I pay cash when it arrives?

b.v: 2) Write the description in layers
People scan, they do not read. Put the reason to buy first, the details second, and the boring specifications last.

Write in this order:|One line on who it is for and what it fixes|Three bullets on the main benefits, in plain words|A short paragraph on what is included|Specifications as a short list|Delivery time and return window, as plain text
Do not copy the supplier description. Everyone sells the same text, so you look like a reseller with no responsibility, and it often contains wrong sizes.
3) Fix the small things that block the sale
The button, the price and the trust line do more work than any paragraph.

v: Price clearly visible without scrolling far
Button text that says something specific, like Add to cart
Cash on delivery stated in one short line near the button
A real photo of the product in use, not only on a white background

b.v: Practice
Rewrite one product page using the five layers above. Then send the link to one friend and ask: what is unclear? Fix that one thing.

day-6.t: Day 6 — Shipping and cash on delivery in Pakistan

b.v: Today's goal

v: Set up shipping rates you can defend
Understand how courier cash on delivery works
Write a delivery promise you can keep

b.v: About 25 minutes. Keep a notebook for actual courier quotes.

In Pakistan most first orders are cash on delivery, usually shortened to COD. The courier collects the cash from the customer and pays you later, minus their charges. The rates change with weight, city and courier, so treat every figure as an example and confirm the current rate.
1) Set shipping in the store
You can charge a flat rate, free shipping, or a rate based on weight. Start simple: one flat rate for the whole country.

Set it up:|Settings, then Shipping and delivery|Create a zone called Pakistan|Add a flat rate and type the amount in PKR|Add a second rate called free over a set order value|Save, then test with a real address at checkout
2) How COD actually works

You book a parcel with a courier that offers COD. They deliver, collect cash, and settle with you on a cycle, usually weekly or on request. Each courier has its own settlement rules, so ask before you promise anything to a customer.

v: Ask for the COD charge per parcel and the settlement day
Ask what happens to the cash if the parcel is refused
Keep your own record of every parcel number
Reconcile the courier statement against your orders weekly

b.v: Do not promise next day delivery across Pakistan. One delayed parcel turns into a public complaint on Facebook, and that comment stays for years.
3) Reduce refused parcels
A refused parcel costs you the forward and return delivery. Two small habits cut this a lot, and both are free.

v: Confirm the order on WhatsApp before dispatch, in one short message
Send a photo of the packed parcel before booking
State the total amount clearly, including delivery
Call first time COD customers in small towns before shipping

b.v: Practice
Call two couriers today and ask for their current COD charge, delivery time to your city and settlement day. Write the answers side by side and pick one.

day-7.t: Day 7 — Payment options and getting paid

b.v: Today's goal

v: Know which payment methods you can actually offer
Set up manual methods honestly
Understand what a payment gateway needs

b.v: About 20 minutes. Do this on a laptop if you can.

Shopify Payments is not available for sellers in Pakistan. That is normal and not a problem: you can still take money through local wallets, bank transfer, and cash on delivery. The important thing is to be clear at checkout about what happens next.
1) Offer what you can support
A payment method is a promise. If you list JazzCash but do not check the number daily, customers will wait and then complain.

v: Cash on delivery, the default for most new stores
JazzCash or Easypaisa transfer, with the transaction ID sent on WhatsApp
Bank transfer for larger orders
Card payments only through a proper gateway, never by asking for card numbers in chat

b.v: 2) Set up manual payment methods
Manual methods are recorded by you, not by an automatic gateway. Customers see your instructions at checkout and pay outside the store.

Add one:|Settings, then Payments|Choose manual payment methods|Add Cash on delivery with a short instruction line|Add a custom method called JazzCash and paste your number|Write exactly what the customer must send you and when|Place a test order to read the confirmation screen
Never ask a customer to send a card number, CVV or PIN on WhatsApp. It is unsafe, it breaks the rules of every payment provider, and it looks like a scam even when you are honest.
3) If you want a gateway later

A payment gateway lets customers pay by card inside checkout. It needs a registered business, a bank account and a verification process, and each provider charges its own fee. Check the current fee and requirements directly with the provider.

v: Ask what documents they need before you apply
Ask about the setup time in writing
Ask the fee per transaction and the settlement delay
Keep COD running alongside cards, most local buyers expect it

b.v: Practice
Add cash on delivery and one wallet method today. Then write the exact WhatsApp message a customer will get after choosing the wallet, and save it as a quick reply.
Today's goal

v: Write four short policy pages in your own words
Make your contact details easy to find
Remove the reasons a stranger would not trust the store

b.v: About 20 minutes. Write plainly, no legal language.
Trust is a page, not a feeling. A shopper who cannot find an address, a phone number or a return rule assumes the worst and leaves. These pages also protect you when a dispute starts.
1) The four pages you need
Keep each one short. Two paragraphs beat two pages that nobody reads.

v: Delivery: how long, which courier, what it costs
Returns and exchanges: the window, the condition, who pays the return
Privacy: what you collect and why, usually name, phone and address
Contact: phone, WhatsApp, email and city

b.v: 2) Write them from real answers
Do not copy another store. Copy the structure, then answer as yourself, because your rules must match what you will really do.

Draft each page:|Write the question a customer would ask|Answer it in one sentence|Add one sentence on what happens if something goes wrong|Add your WhatsApp number at the bottom|Publish and link it in the footer menu
Do not write a seven day return policy if you cannot afford returns. A policy you break costs more trust than a stricter policy you keep.
3) Small trust signals that cost nothing
These take minutes and quietly answer the question: is this a real shop?

v: A photo of your actual packaging, not a stock photo
A city name in the footer
A working phone number, answered during stated hours
Reviews from real orders only, with the buyer's permission

b.v: Practice
Publish all four pages today and add them to the footer. Then ask a family member to find your return policy in under twenty seconds.

day-9.t: Day 9 — Your first traffic without burning money

b.v: Today's goal

v: Get your first visitors without an ad budget
Prepare one product for a small paid test
Know the number that tells you to stop

b.v: About 25 minutes. Phone camera and WhatsApp are enough.
Nobody buys from a store nobody visits. But paying for traffic before the product page works is the fastest way to lose money. Start with free reach, fix the page, then pay for a small test.
1) Free reach that still works
You are looking for the first ten orders, not a brand. Ten real customers teach you more than a thousand visitors.

v: Your own WhatsApp status, posted twice a day with a real photo
Facebook groups where selling is allowed, read the rules first
Local WhatsApp groups for your city or community
Friends of friends, ask for a share not a purchase

b.v: 2) Prepare before you pay for clicks
A small test only teaches you something if the page is ready. Fix these four first.
Checklist before any ad:|Three clear photos and one short video|Price and delivery charge visible without scrolling|COD mentioned near the button|A test order placed by you, start to finish
Do not boost a post just because the button is easy to press. A boosted post without a target audience and a clear offer spends money and teaches nothing.
3) Run one small honest test
Set a budget you can lose without pain, run it for a few days, and judge it on orders, not on likes.

v: Pick one audience, not five
Write the ad as a message to one person
Decide your stop rule before you start
Count messages and orders, not views

b.v: Practice
Post one product on your WhatsApp status and in one allowed group today. Write down how many people asked the price. That number is your first real signal.

day-10.t: Day 10 — Read your analytics and fix one thing

b.v: Today's goal

v: Read the four numbers that matter
Find where customers drop off
Choose one fix for next week

b.v: About 20 minutes. Open your Shopify analytics.
Analytics is not a report card, it is a map of where money leaks. You do not need every chart. Four numbers tell you most of the story in a small store.
1) The four numbers
Learn these in plain words first, then look at the charts.

v: Visitors = how many people opened the store
Add to cart rate = how many put something in the basket
Conversion rate = orders divided by visitors, shown as a percentage
Average order value = total sales divided by number of orders

b.v: 2) Find the leak
Each drop-off point has a different fix. Guessing wastes weeks, so match the symptom to the cause.

Diagnose like this:|Many visitors, few add to cart, check photos and price|Many add to cart, few checkouts, check delivery charge and trust lines|Many checkouts, few delivered, check COD confirmation and courier|Many orders, low profit, check your cost sheet again
Do not change five things in one week. You will not know which change helped, and you will probably keep the wrong one.
3) Write a weekly review in ten minutes
Same day every week, same four numbers, one decision. That habit is the whole skill.

v: Orders this week versus last week
Money collected minus money spent
Best selling product and worst selling product
One thing to fix, written as a task with a date

b.v: Practice
Write your four numbers for this week in a notebook. Then pick the single weakest one and write the fix you will do in the next seven days.
